## Findings (2)

**`/home/afief/Developer/wordlex/apps/play/src/lib/board-snapshot.ts:12` — low.** The comment justifying the dropped Answer ("the read every mount fires brings it back well before the rollover") assumes that read succeeds, but the snapshot exists precisely for when it doesn't. Concrete scenario: a player loses a board, goes offline, and keeps/reopens the tab across the WIB rollover. The mount read fails; `retry: false` and `refetchOnReconnect: false` in `router.tsx:24` mean there is no second attempt, and because a snapshot board is on screen, `problem` in `use-game.ts:235-238` stays `undefined`, so no error and no retry button is shown either. `result-sheet.tsx:101-106` flips `dayOver` to true at midnight, but `board.answer` is still `undefined`, so the Answer line at `:151` silently never renders. Before this change the snapshot carried the Answer and it would have appeared.

The scope is genuinely narrow and worth stating in the comment rather than leaving the guarantee absolute: on a fresh restore `dayOver` is always false (`readBoardSnapshot` deletes any snapshot whose `day !== wordlexDay()`, so `dayEndsAt(board.day)` is always in the future), and won boards lose nothing (`:151` gates on `!won`, and a won board's answer is its last guess, already on the board). The only exposed case is a lost/abandoned board whose read fails across the rollover.

**`/home/afief/Developer/wordlex/docs/board-offline-cache-design.md:22` — low.** Same overstatement, in the doc that future readers will trust: "the read every mount fires brings the Answer back in time for the rollover that reveals it" is stated unconditionally. With `retry: false` and `refetchOnReconnect: false`, a failed mount read is never retried automatically, so the sentence should say the Answer comes back *when that read succeeds*, and note that an offline session crossing the rollover will not show it.

## What I checked and did not file

- `Omit<Board, "answer">` does not structurally forbid an `answer` property, so `StoredBoard` documents an invariant it doesn't enforce — but the writer strips it unconditionally, so there is no scenario where the code misbehaves.
- `PREFIX`/`version` were not bumped despite the shape change — it works, because the new shape is a strict subset and the `"answer" in board` rejection plus `removeItem` makes old snapshots self-heal into a network read.
- `readBoardSnapshot` returning `StoredBoard` into a `Board`-typed query's `initialData` compiles cleanly (`answer` is optional); `apps/play` typechecks with no errors.
- `board.answer` is read in exactly one place (`result-sheet.tsx:151-152`); `shareText` does not use it.</result>
